I will keep my land in the pattern I know best. I have farmed for 40 years, I have well irrigation, and at my age I do not want to gamble on complicated changes. In winter, I will put all 20.4 mu into wheat because that is the base of my wheat-maize system and it fits my land and water conditions. After wheat harvest, I will put most of the summer land into maize because maize gives me the main grain output and works well after wheat, and I will keep a smaller part in millet because millet is familiar to me, needs less water and fertilizer, and spreads my risk. Since some family members work off-farm, I will choose a management style that is steady and not too labor-heavy: improved or hybrid seed, medium fertilizer rates, limited but timely irrigation from the well, a small number of pesticide sprays, and simple tillage methods that I can manage without making the work too heavy. I am not chasing the very highest yield; I am choosing a stable yield with work I can finish on time.
